title: Count of Siruela, Spanish ambassador at Genoa, to Philip IV, 19 May 1638 (catalogue 755): money for munitions and the Marquis Pallavicino

steps.what: Inventory of the 20 shelfmarks of no. 755 and survey of neighbouring PARES records: most 1638 letters have their plain copy.
Key rebuilt on 146/145, 143/142, 169/168 (cipher aligned on contemporary plain copies), frozen before each test.
Held-out tests on 169 and 158: significant but below the pre-set criterion (0.85 chars / 0.75 words); reported.
Final held-out test 160 vs plain copy 159: 0.896 chars / 0.784 words vs control p99 0.343 / 0.204.
3594,156 transcribed and read with K3f (+ hnf = Vuestra Majestad).

validation.notes: The key was validated in the target's own pre-registered held-out test (3594,160 against its clear copy 3594,159: 0.896 of characters, 0.784 of words; 200 permuted-value controls at the 99th percentile 0.343 and 0.204); the n-gram validator was not rerun.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from other letters of the same cipher with their contemporary plain copies, validated on a held-out pair, then applied to 3594,156.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 94 words in the cipher portion (“V. M.” counted as two): 89 certain, 3 probable (marqués, me, faltando), 1 restored from the sense (haciendo), 1 unresolved (code 197).

credits.note: key rebuilt and validated on a held-out pair; 3594,156 read, Spanish text and English translation

texts.label: Count of Siruela to Philip IV, Genoa, 19 May 1638 (AGS EST,LEG,3594,156)
texts.summary: In the spring of 1638 the Spanish ambassador at Genoa had to lay in munitions on the spot. The King had ordered the Marquis Pablo Jerónimo Pallavicino (“Palavesín”) to advance him the money; the Marquis was stalling. Velasco told the King in cipher: if he failed his suppliers, they would fail him in turn.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 31 Oct 2026: coherent Spanish dispatch (Palavesín delaying the royal order on munitions money); one unresolved group (197, a name) and a few {probable} words, scattered.

texts.label: Validation letter AGS EST,LEG,3594,160 (contemporary clear copy 3594,159)
texts.summary: A held-out cipher letter of the same ambassador, 19 May 1638, kept apart while the key was built and then read with the frozen key against its contemporary clear copy 3594,159; used only to test the key, not a reading of ours.

prior.where: Catalogue 755 open; no target folder in this repository; no plain copy of 3594,156 in the bundle (PARES survey 28 Oct 2026).

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
